_meta.description: Curated seed knowledge base of Indian welfare schemes for Yojana Saathi.
_meta.disclaimer: Benefit amounts and rules change. Always verify on the official portal before applying. Refresh this file from https://www.myscheme.gov.in and official scheme sites.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
schemes.summary: Direct income support for landholding farmer families, paid into the bank account through DBT.
schemes.benefits: Rs 6,000 per year paid in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 each, directly to the farmer family's Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
schemes.eligibility: Landholding farmer families whose names appear in land records. Excluded: institutional landholders, families where any member is an income-tax payer, serving or retired government employees (except Group D / multi-tasking staff), constitutional post holders, and professionals such as doctors, engineers, lawyers and CAs practising their profession.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register on the PM-KISAN portal (New Farmer Registration), at a Common Service Centre (CSC), or through the village revenue officer / agriculture department. Complete e-KYC with OTP or biometrics.

schemes.name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana)
schemes.summary: Free cashless health insurance for poor and vulnerable families at empanelled public and private hospitals.
schemes.benefits: Health cover of up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation, cashless and paperless at empanelled hospitals. Senior citizens aged 70 and above are covered regardless of income under the Ayushman Vay Vandana extension.
schemes.eligibility: Families identified as deprived under SECC 2011 criteria (rural) or occupational categories (urban), families covered under state-linked lists such as ration-card based lists, and all citizens aged 70 years and above irrespective of income.
schemes.how_to_apply: Check eligibility on the PM-JAY beneficiary portal or the Ayushman app, then get the Ayushman card made at a CSC or an empanelled hospital's Arogya Mitra desk.

schemes.name: PM Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)
schemes.summary: Deposit-free LPG connections for women from poor households to replace polluting cooking fuels.
schemes.benefits: Deposit-free LPG connection with first refill support, and a targeted subsidy on refills credited to the bank account.
schemes.eligibility: Adult women (18+) from poor households (BPL, SC/ST, PMAY-G, Antyodaya and similar lists) with no existing LPG connection in the household.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply online on the PMUY portal or at the nearest LPG distributor (Indane, Bharat Gas, HP Gas).

schemes.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY)
schemes.summary: High-interest, tax-free small-savings account for the education and marriage of a girl child.
schemes.benefits: Government-notified interest rate (revised quarterly), tax deduction under Section 80C, and tax-free maturity. Minimum deposit Rs 250 and maximum Rs 1.5 lakh per financial year.
schemes.eligibility: Parent or legal guardian of a girl child below 10 years of age. Up to two accounts per family (three in case of twins/triplets).
documents: Birth certificate of the girl child
schemes.how_to_apply: Open the account at any post office or authorised bank branch.

schemes.name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
schemes.summary: Guaranteed pension scheme mainly for unorganised-sector workers.
schemes.benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 from age 60 depending on contribution; the same pension to the spouse after the subscriber's death, and the corpus to the nominee.
schemes.eligibility: Indian citizens aged 18 to 40 years with a savings bank account. Income-tax payers are not eligible (from 1 October 2022).
schemes.how_to_apply: Through your bank branch or net banking; contributions are auto-debited.

schemes.name: PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
schemes.summary: Low-cost one-year renewable life insurance.
schemes.benefits: Life cover of Rs 2 lakh for death due to any reason, for an annual premium of Rs 436 auto-debited from the bank account.
schemes.eligibility: People aged 18 to 50 years with a savings bank or post office account who give consent for auto-debit.
schemes.how_to_apply: Enrol through your bank branch, net banking or the Jan Suraksha portal.

schemes.name: PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)
schemes.summary: Very low-cost accident insurance.
schemes.benefits: Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or total permanent disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial permanent disability, for an annual premium of Rs 20.
schemes.eligibility: People aged 18 to 70 years with a savings bank or post office account.
schemes.how_to_apply: Enrol through your bank branch, net banking or the Jan Suraksha portal.

schemes.name: Mahatma Gandhi NREGA (Rural Employment Guarantee)
schemes.summary: Legal guarantee of wage employment for rural households.
schemes.benefits: At least 100 days of guaranteed unskilled manual work per rural household per financial year at notified state wage rates, paid to the bank/post office account. Unemployment allowance if work is not provided within 15 days of demand.
schemes.eligibility: Adult members of any rural household willing to do unskilled manual work.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply for a job card at the Gram Panchayat, then submit a written or oral demand for work.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY - Gramin & Urban 2.0)
schemes.summary: Financial assistance to build or buy a pucca house for houseless families and those living in kutcha houses.
schemes.benefits: Gramin: financial assistance for house construction in instalments plus convergence support (toilet, MGNREGA work days). Urban 2.0: central assistance for construction, affordable rental housing, or interest subsidy on home loans for EWS/LIG/MIG families.
schemes.eligibility: Families without a pucca house anywhere in India. Urban 2.0 income bands: EWS up to Rs 3 lakh, LIG up to Rs 6 lakh and MIG up to Rs 9 lakh annual household income.
documents: Self-declaration of not owning a pucca house
schemes.how_to_apply: Gramin: beneficiaries are selected through Gram Sabha verification; contact the Gram Panchayat. Urban: apply on the PMAY-U 2.0 portal or at the urban local body.

schemes.name: PM Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)
schemes.summary: Maternity cash benefit to support nutrition and wage loss for pregnant and lactating mothers.
schemes.benefits: Rs 5,000 in instalments for the first child, and Rs 6,000 for the second child if the second child is a girl, paid by DBT.
schemes.eligibility: Pregnant women and lactating mothers, excluding those in regular employment with central/state government or PSUs.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register through the Anganwadi worker / ASHA or on the PMMVY portal.

schemes.name: PM Vishwakarma
schemes.summary: End-to-end support for traditional artisans and craftspeople in 18 trades (carpenters, potters, tailors, blacksmiths, cobblers, barbers and more).
schemes.benefits: PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID card, skill training with daily stipend, toolkit incentive of up to Rs 15,000, collateral-free credit of up to Rs 3 lakh in two tranches at a concessional interest rate, and digital and marketing support.
schemes.eligibility: Artisans aged 18+ working with hands and tools in one of the 18 listed family-based trades, self-employed in the unorganised sector. Government employees and their families are not eligible.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register through a Common Service Centre (CSC) with biometric Aadhaar authentication; verified by the Gram Panchayat / ULB.

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
schemes.summary: Collateral-free working-capital loans for street vendors, with incentives for timely repayment and digital payments.
schemes.benefits: Collateral-free working-capital loans in increasing tranches, interest subsidy on timely repayment, and cashback on digital transactions.
schemes.eligibility: Street vendors in urban areas holding a vending certificate / ID from the urban local body, or identified in the ULB survey, or with a Letter of Recommendation.
documents: Vending certificate or Letter of Recommendation
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply on the PM SVANidhi portal, through a CSC, or via a lending bank / urban local body.

schemes.name: Stand-Up India
schemes.summary: Bank loans for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs to start a new (greenfield) enterprise.
schemes.benefits: Bank loans between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore for setting up a greenfield enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied activities, with handholding support.
schemes.eligibility: SC/ST and/or women entrepreneurs aged 18+. For non-individual enterprises, at least 51% shareholding must be held by an SC/ST or woman entrepreneur. Borrower must not be in default with any bank.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply on the Stand-Up India portal or directly at a scheduled commercial bank branch.

schemes.name: Post-Matric Scholarship for SC Students
schemes.summary: Scholarship for Scheduled Caste students studying beyond Class 10.
schemes.benefits: Covers compulsory non-refundable fees and an academic allowance for post-matric and higher education courses, paid by DBT.
schemes.eligibility: Scheduled Caste students studying in Class 11 and above (including UG, PG and diploma courses) whose parents' annual income is up to Rs 2.5 lakh.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal (or the state scholarship portal, e.g. SSP Karnataka) during the open application window.

schemes.name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (NSAP)
schemes.summary: Monthly pension for elderly people from BPL households.
schemes.benefits: Monthly pension with a central contribution, topped up by the state government (in Karnataka paid through Sandhya Suraksha / old-age pension schemes).
schemes.eligibility: Persons aged 60 years and above belonging to BPL households.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply at the Gram Panchayat / taluk office or through Nadakacheri / Seva Sindhu in Karnataka.

schemes.name: Gruha Lakshmi (Karnataka)
schemes.summary: Monthly financial assistance to the woman head of the family in Karnataka.
schemes.benefits: Rs 2,000 per month transferred to the bank account of the woman head of the family.
schemes.eligibility: Woman recorded as head of the family on the ration card (APL, BPL or Antyodaya) and a resident of Karnataka. Not eligible if the woman or her husband is an income-tax payer or GST filer, or a government employee.
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the Seva Sindhu portal, Grama One, Karnataka One or Bapuji Seva Kendras.

schemes.name: Shakti (Karnataka)
schemes.summary: Free bus travel for women in Karnataka.
schemes.benefits: Free travel for women (and transgender persons) in non-premium state transport buses (KSRTC, BMTC, KKRTC, NWKRTC) within Karnataka.
schemes.eligibility: Women and transgender persons who are residents of Karnataka.
documents: Any government ID with Karnataka address (e.g. Aadhaar)
schemes.how_to_apply: No application needed for travel; show a valid Karnataka ID to the conductor and get a zero-fare ticket.

schemes.name: Gruha Jyothi (Karnataka)
schemes.summary: Free household electricity up to an eligible limit in Karnataka.
schemes.benefits: Free electricity for domestic consumers up to their eligible limit, based on the household's average monthly consumption plus a margin, capped at 200 units per month.
schemes.eligibility: Domestic electricity consumers (residential connections) in Karnataka; one connection per registered household.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register on the Seva Sindhu portal or at Grama One / Karnataka One / Bangalore One centres.

schemes.name: Anna Bhagya (Karnataka)
schemes.summary: Food grain support for BPL and Antyodaya ration-card households in Karnataka.
schemes.benefits: Free rice through the public distribution system for each member of BPL and Antyodaya households, with the state's additional entitlement provided as grains or cash transfer as notified.
schemes.eligibility: Households holding a BPL (Priority Household) or Antyodaya Anna Yojana ration card in Karnataka.
schemes.how_to_apply: Benefits come automatically to eligible ration cards; apply for a ration card through the Ahara (Food) department portal if you do not have one.

schemes.name: Yuva Nidhi (Karnataka)
schemes.summary: Unemployment allowance for recent graduates and diploma holders in Karnataka.
schemes.benefits: Rs 3,000 per month for unemployed graduates and Rs 1,500 per month for unemployed diploma holders, for up to two years or until they get a job, whichever is earlier.
schemes.eligibility: Karnataka-domiciled graduates or diploma holders who passed out in 2022-23 or later and have not found employment (including self-employment) within 180 days of graduating, and who are not pursuing higher studies.
schemes.how_to_apply: Register on the Seva Sindhu portal and submit a self-declaration of unemployment every month.
